title: Professional Summary
text:
My undergraduate journey was not a straight path. I explored several fields, including creative writing, political science, and computer science, before ultimately finding the discipline that brought together my interests: statistics. That process required a great deal of self-reflection, and it helped me recognize that I wanted to pursue work centered around understanding the world through evidence, analysis, and careful reasoning.
Throughout my degree, I built a foundation across mathematical theory, programming, statistical reasoning, and real-world applications. Beyond the classroom, I applied these skills through experiences in public health, workplace operations, and community research, including work with Public Health AmeriCorps, the Plemmons Student Union, and AppHealthCare. I also developed my communication skills as an Opinion writer for The Appalachian, where I explored issues through research and writing.
I graduated with a broad understanding of statistics and its applications, along with the ability to combine quantitative analysis, clear communication, and collaborative problem-solving to address meaningful questions.

Academic and Professional Highlights

YRBS Data Analysis
I worked with Youth Risk Behavior Survey data to uncover patterns in student health behaviors and develop tools that made the data more useful for local decision-making. By building automated workflows and clear visualizations in R, I helped our team translate raw survey data into actionable insights for schools and community partners.


Public Health AmeriCorps
I contributed to rural public health initiatives focused on improving community resilience, emergency preparedness, and health equity. Through this work, I gained insight into how research, and evidence-based interventions can support communities facing complex health challenges.


Plemmons Student Union
I began my work at the Plemmons Student Union as an Operations Assistant, and was promoted to Student Supervisor where I led student employees, supported daily operations, and developed leadership and team management skills. I then had the opportunity to apply my statistical background to ongoing projects. I collected data and analyzed employee experiences to improve workplace processes. Through this experience, I gained insight into how data informs industrial-organizational psychology. I also prepared a report based on my findings to inform management of shift disparities, leading to a change in workplace policy.


The Appalachian Opinion Desk
I developed my writing and research skills at The Appalachian, where I explored complex topics and communicated ideas clearly for a broad audience. Through this experience, I learned to work within publication guidelines, conduct thorough research, and translate nuanced issues into accessible and engaging pieces for readers.

I am a recent graduate of Appalachian State University with a B.S. in Mathematics, concentrating in Statistics. My interest in statistics comes from its unique ability to uncover patterns, challenge assumptions, and bring clarity to complex issues.
My work is driven by curiosity and a belief that understanding is the foundation of improvement. Statistics provides a universal language for exploring everything from scientific research to social issues, allowing us to transform questions into knowledge and knowledge into action.
On this site, you’ll find my resume, statistical work samples, writing from my time at The Appalachian and beyond, and some of the creative pursuits I enjoy outside of my professional work. Thanks for stopping by!

Areas of Interest



Public Policy
Addressing complex societal challenges by using research and evidence to evaluate solutions, inform decision-making, and improve outcomes in areas such as immigration, healthcare, and economics.



Healthcare Research
Improving health equity and uncover insights that can improve care for underserved populations. I’m excited about leveraging data to answer complex questions and better measure healthcare outcomes.

title: Data Analysis Work Samples
text:
Click the links below to explore selected work samples!

Data Analysis Projects

Time Series Analysis in R
Examined time series data of energy generation and cryptocurrency volatility. This project showcases skills in time series modeling, model comparisons, model diagnostics, model interpretation, forecasting, handling seasonality in time series data, and data visualization.
View Project →


College Football Predictive Modeling in R
Built an expanded dataset from an existing R package and used statistical modeling to predict team win probabilities. This project showcases skills in data collection, cleaning, feature engineering, visualization, model selection, and predictive modeling techniques including logistic regression, ridge regression, decision trees, and K-nearest neighbors.
View Project →
View Presentation →


Home Prices Analysis in R
Modeled home prices in King County based on various explanatory variables. This project showcases skills in data collection, exploratory analysis, linear regression, ridge regression, subset selection, data visualization, model diagnostics, and transformation.
View Project →


Charlotte MLB Viability Analysis in R
Built a multi-source dataset and used linear regression to assess Charlotte’s viability as a potential MLB market. This project showcases data collection, data cleaning, linear regression, predictive modeling, feature engineering, and data visualization.
View Project →


Horror Movie Analysis in Python
Used APIs and web scraping to compare performance of horror movies across metrics based on selected variables. This project showcases web scraping, API usage, data cleaning, Python library usage, hypothesis testing, and data visualization.
View Presentation →
